settings.name_in_paper: Online strategic classification against delta-bounded myopically rational (delta-BMR) agents, Stackelberg regret
unmapped: Learner's actions are linear classifiers (hyperplane normals) in A subset of [-1,1]^{d+1}; binary 0-1 loss on the agent's reported feature vector

Agents best-respond to the committed classifier by misreporting within a ball of radius delta around a hidden, adversarially chosen feature vector (delta-BMR); utility unknown to learner; delta known to learner
Feedback: the learner observes the reported vector r_t(alpha_t) and label y_t, from which she infers losses of all actions whose hyperplane is far (>2 delta) from r_t (induced feedback graph)
Regret is Stackelberg regret: comparator evaluated on agents' best responses to the comparator
Algorithm requires an in-probability oracle and polytope volume computations

symbols.rho: lambda(A)/lambda(underline p_delta): ratio of the Lebesgue measure of the action space to that of the smallest polytope induced by Grinder after T rounds

tuning: eta = gamma <= 1/2, tuned as in the analysis (depends on T and lambda(underline p))

source.label: thm:regr-grind
source.quote: Given a finite horizon $T$ the Stackelberg regret incurred by $\grinder$ (Algo.~\ref{algo:grinding}) is: \calR(T) \leq \calO ( \sqrt{T \cdot \log (T\cdot\frac{\lambda( \calA )}{\lambda(\up)}) \cdot \log (\frac{\lambda( \calA )}{\lambda(\up)})}) where by $\lambda(A)$ we denote the Lebesgue measure ... and by $\up$ we denote the polytope with the smallest Lebesgue measure that is induced by $\grinder$ after $T$ rounds' partition.

results.notes: Proof takes expectations over the algorithm's sampling, so regret is effectively in expectation, but the theorem states R(T) without stating the type. Paper says Grinder is information-theoretic (polytope volume #P-hard); with a volume oracle runtime O(T^d). Data-dependent bound.

symbols.C_0: unspecified constant hidden in the O(.) of the first term
symbols.eps_alg: multiplicative approximation accuracy of the in-probability oracle

conditions: eps-approximate in-probability oracle with eps <= 1/2: |P~[alpha] - P^in[alpha]| <= eps P^in[alpha]
tuning: eta = gamma tuned as in Theorem 4.1

source.label: lem:apx-oracle
source.quote: For $\eps \leq 1/2$, we call $\tPr_t[\alpha_t]$ an $\eps$-approximation oracle to $\Prin[\alpha_t]$, if $|\tPr_t [\alpha_t] - \Prin[\alpha_t] | \leq \eps \Prin[\alpha_t]$. Then, $\grinder$ run with oracle $\tPr_t[\cdot]$ instead of $\Prin[\alpha_t]$ achieves Stackelberg regret $\calR(T) \leq \calO(\sqrt{ T \log (T \lambda(\calA)/\lambda(\up))\cdot \log (\lambda(\calA)/\lambda(\up))}) + 2 \eps T$.

results.notes: Mixed O-term plus explicit 2 eps T; encoded with constant C_0. Paper notes the rate is preserved for eps <= 1/sqrt(T).

symbols.rho_tilde: lambda(A)/lambda(tilde p_delta), where tilde p_delta is the smallest sigma_t-induced polytope from the sequence of datapoints

conditions: hard instance uses truthful agents (a special case of delta-BMR) with labels drawn from Bernoulli environments

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: For any strategy and any $\delta$, there exists a sequence of $\{\sigma_t\}_{t = 1}^T$ such that: \E [ \sum_{t \in [T]} \ell(\alpha_t, \vr_t(\alpha_t),y_t) ] - \min_{\alphast \in \calA} \E [ \sum_{t \in [T]} \ell(\alphast, \vr_t(\alphast),y_t)] \geq \frac{1}{9\sqrt{2}} \sqrt{T \log ( \frac{\lambda(\calA)}{\lambda(\tp)})} where $\tp$ is the smallest $\sigma_t$-induced polytope from the sequence of $\{\sigma_t\}_{t=1}^T$.

results.notes: Min taken outside expectation, so pseudo-regret style. Nearly matches Theorem 4.1 up to a sqrt(log) factor.

conditions: fixed truthful agents with feature vector x=(u)^d, u in [1/4,3/4]; labels i.i.d. Bernoulli under one of two environments U, L

source.label: lem:sqrt
source.quote: Fix a $\vr = \vx = (u)^d$ ... There exists a utility model for the agents, and a pair of adversarial environments $U$ and $L$ such that $\vr_t(\alpha) = \vx_t = \vx$ ... such that: \max_{\nu \in \{U,L\}} \min_{\alphast \in \calA} \E_{\nu} [\sum_{t} \ell(\alpha_t, \vr_t(\alpha_t),y_t) - \sum_{t} \ell(\alphast,\vr_t(\alphast),y_t) ] \geq \frac{1}{9\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{T}

results.notes: Building block of Theorem 5.1. Theorem 3.3 (incompatibility of external and Stackelberg regret: linear regret in one notion) not recorded as it gives no explicit bound expression.
